text:
Maya (support): FYI - escalation from AcmeCorp, multiple API 5xx/timeouts on hosted inference since ~07:12 UTC. They report high error rates and timeouts for generation endpoints. I can repro in our staging account too.

Maya (support): Error payload from the client: `HTTP 504 gateway_timeout` and sometimes `HTTP 502 bad_gateway` with stack hint `kv/prefix-cache` in the stack. Customer says errors spike when they hit a certain prompt set.

Maya (support): Quick log snippet from frontend proxy: ```ERROR transport: upstream response error: code=502 msg="redis: connection timeout" route=/v1/generate```.

incident-bot: Alert: service=redwood-prefix-cache severity=warning count=72 last=07:18 UTC (see /alerts/12345).

Raj (sre): Looking. Do we have redis cluster errors/latency graphs? Can you paste the exact request IDs? Need to correlate trace.

Maya (support): Two sample request ids: `req_0a9f2b`, `req_0a9f81`. I pulled a bit more logs from the gateway: ```[2024-04-14T07:12:23Z] req=req_0a9f2b route=/v1/generate cache.get prefix=k:acme:user:123 err="dial tcp 10.2.1.5:6379: i/o timeout"```

Lena (eng-runtime): That looks like the prefix cache (redis) client can't reach nodes. Any recent deploys to the cache pool or infra changes?

Ben (oncall): I didn't push cache infra changes. I see elevated connection_timeouts in the redis metrics around 07:10 - 07:20 UTC. Memory/evictions look normal. Network retransmits spiked for nodes in us-east-1a. Possibly an AZ networking flake affecting the managed redis cluster.

Tom (cs): Customer impact: ~25% of requests failing for them. They're asking for ETA and mitigation. They're asking for credits if this persists.

Raj (sre): Short term mitigation: 1) Disable prefix/KV caching for hosted inference routes for affected customers so requests bypass redis and hit cold store. 2) Add temporary circuit-breaker to avoid gateway 5xxs and respond with graceful retry. Will coordinate a quick config change and rollback if it causes regression.

Lena (eng-runtime): I can prepare the route config toggle. Setting `prefix_cache.enabled=false` on their tenant route should route around the cache. On our side, it's a per-tenant config in route-manifest.

Ben (oncall): Doing it now for tenant `acme-prod` -> patching route manifest. Command: ```kubectl -n routes exec deploy/route-configurator -- curl -s -X PATCH http://localhost/tenants/acme-prod -d '{"prefix_cache":{"enabled":false}}'```

Ben (oncall): Patch applied. A couple of seconds later metrics: prefix_cache.errors down from 60/min to ~2/min, gateway 5xxs for that tenant dropped to near zero. Will continue monitoring for 15m. :thumbsup:

Maya (support): Verified with customer — error rate dropped to normal. They still see slightly higher latency but it's functional. Customer asked for root-cause and next steps.

Raj (sre): We're assuming root cause is transient network instability in us-east-1 AZ impacting the managed redis nodes. Action items: 1) Engage infra provider (redis/managed service) — open ticket with logs. 2) Consider moving critical prefix-cache shards out of the affected AZ / promote replicas. 3) Improve our fallback: make bypassing prefix cache automated when cache errors >= threshold (circuit-breaker). 4) Postmortem after stable.

Lena (eng-runtime): I'll open a PR to add an automatic cache-fallback feature: config defaults to `fail-open=false`, but we'll add `auto_fail_open_threshold=5m/err_rate>20%` toggle and a metric that triggers route-level bypass.

Tom (cs): I'll draft a customer-facing note and offer credits per SLO.

Ben (oncall): Follow-up checks: redis cluster shows 3/6 nodes with elevated tcp_retransmits and connection resets. Node restart attempted by provider at 07:25 UTC and seemed to recover by 07:40 UTC. Will attach provider ticket.

Maya (support): Filed support case for AcmeCorp and sent update: "We routed your requests around a degraded cache backend; our engineering team is investigating root cause. We'll follow up with details and remediation timeline."

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-042 (prefix-cache outage affecting hosted inference). Severity: high. Lead: Raj.

Raj (sre): Assigning postmortem owner. I'll start the incident doc and collect traces: link /incidents/INC-2024-042. Please paste any related logs/trace snippets here.

Maya (support): Adding the two requests + reproduction steps: 1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"<customer prompt batch>","max_tokens":256}' 2) Observe intermittent 502/504 within 500-1000 requests.

Lena (eng-runtime): Noted. Also will put in short-term guardrails so hosting routes degrade gracefully instead of surfacing the raw backend errors.

Tom (cs): Customer ask: timeline for permanent fix and whether we can guarantee it won't happen again. I'll coordinate comms after root cause confirmed.

Ben (oncall): Monitoring window complete (20m). No reoccurrence after provider restart and our route bypass. Closing immediate incident; keeping incident doc open for RCA follow-up.

Maya (support): Closing loop with customer and offering 10% monthly credit for the affected window. They accepted provisional credit and asked for postmortem.

Raj (sre): Postmortem tasks assigned. Will include timeline, provider ticket, infra changes, and the feature PR for auto-fail-open.

Lena (eng-runtime): I'll link the feature PR and a suggested rollout plan for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Maya (support): Thanks everyone. :heart:
